answer.what_it_does: Atlassian Rovo agents are context-aware AI agents that synthesize organizational knowledge and automate multi-step work across Atlassian apps and connected third-party apps. They can help teams find answers, create or refine content, and handle repetitive tasks using Atlassian’s Teamwork Graph and connected data sources.

incidents_or_risks.what: Atlassian states that it performs safety screening on agents at its discretion for customer protection.
App-based agents only have access to data in the workspace where the app is installed, so access is constrained by installation scope rather than broad automatic access.
Rovo usage consumes Rovo credits, and admins can adjust settings and limits, creating a governance and cost-control consideration for heavy AI use.

facts.claim: Rovo is Atlassian’s AI offering for finding personalized answers, automating tasks, and making smarter decisions using connected organizational context.
Rovo is powered by the Teamwork Graph, which maps relationships across people, apps, projects, code, decisions, and assets.
Rovo agents are designed to handle specific tasks and automate multi-step work across Atlassian and connected apps.
Rovo agents can use data from Atlassian apps and connected third-party apps.
Rovo is available across Atlassian apps, the browser extension, and other work surfaces.
To fully use Search, Chat, Agents, and Studio, an Atlassian Cloud Standard, Premium, or Enterprise plan is required.
Rovo credits are Atlassian’s unit for AI usage and enriched Teamwork Graph API access.

answer.what_it_does: Atlassian Rovo agents are configurable AI teammates that teams can call on to collaborate and move work forward. Based on their configured knowledge sources and enabled tools/skills, Rovo agents can retrieve information from Atlassian and connected third-party apps and, where permitted, perform actions in those systems on the user’s behalf.

ai_agents.name: Rovo agents (platform capability)
ai_agents.what_it_does: Operate as configurable AI teammates that can access configured Atlassian and connected third-party data (subject to permissions) and use enabled tools/skills to carry out work actions in-app and via connected integrations.
actions: Use connected plugins and access data from Atlassian and connected third-party apps (governed by knowledge sources and user/organization permissions).
Perform work actions by invoking skills (reusable, task-oriented capabilities such as creating work items, drafting status updates, or analyzing incident data).
Use tools (individual executable actions) and orchestrate multi-step workflows via skills.
Execute actions with confirmation/approval depending on the tool/skill configuration.
Support custom tool modules published via Atlassian Forge so user-created agents can use capabilities beyond base Chat (within the app/tool permissions).
(In automation contexts) run agent actions as part of automation rules using permissions granted by admins.
Optionally interact with external AI ecosystems via Rovo MCP server / Agent2Agent, subject to admin-controlled domain allowlists and app permissions.

ai_agents.name: Skills (capability layer used by Rovo agents)
ai_agents.what_it_does: Provide the concrete, reusable “work-based actions” that agents can execute (e.g., creating work items, drafting status updates, analyzing incident data) by packaging instructions that Rovo can invoke through the agent/chat/automation experience.
actions: Create work items (Jira/Atlassian work actions, depending on enabled skills and permissions).
Draft status updates (written communication outputs tied to org/work context).
Analyze incident data (incident/workflow assistance where incident data is available via configured sources).
Invoke MCP tools when MCP tools/third-party skills are connected and approved/enabled for the site.

ai_agents.name: Tools (capability layer used by Rovo agents)
ai_agents.what_it_does: Represent the underlying executable capabilities that Rovo agents can call; tools may be Atlassian-provided, third-party, or organization-published and can enable actions outside Chat when configured.
actions: Run individual executable actions (tools) that skills can orchestrate into workflows.
Connect tools to allow an agent to act outside an Atlassian app (when configured).
Use Forge-published tool modules for user-created agents so they can access data/capabilities available to the app/tool module.
Respect visibility/scope rules for where tool modules appear (organization or Atlassian Marketplace publication, based on how the tool is published).

use_cases.name: External AI tool/agent collaboration via Rovo MCP / Agent2Agent (admin-governed)

Third-party agents calling Rovo via Agent2Agent only when enabled by org admins and within the context of data the user is permitted to view.

incidents_or_risks.what: Prompt injection / tool-mediated exfiltration risk where research reports describe paths that could lead to Jira/Confluence data exfiltration when an agent is tricked into using retrieval/tooling and making outbound requests.
incidents_or_risks.when: Recently disclosed (2026 timeframe referenced by the reporting organization; specific dates vary by disclosure path).

incidents_or_risks.what: Cross-user / cross-tenant isolation failure risk reported by third-party discussion (claims of one user/tenant accessing another’s Rovo context), described as a critical finding in the discussion source.
incidents_or_risks.when: Recently reported (published ~last month on the discussion platform).

facts.claim: Rovo agents can be accessed in Chat, automation rules, within Jira/Confluence via shortcut commands, and in Studio.
Skills are reusable instructions that let Rovo Chat and agents carry out specific work-based actions (e.g., creating work items, drafting status updates, analyzing incident data).
Agents can access data from other Atlassian and connected third-party apps depending on their knowledge sources, and they respect user permissions (no cross-site access to unauthorized users).
Admins can control knowledge scope/sites an agent can access (e.g., Unit-wide scope vs configuring specific sites).

Rovo agents are powered by large language model providers including OpenAI and Google (and related open-source and other ML models), and the system uses those models to analyze prompts and generate responses with relevant information from Atlassian and connected third-party products.

answer.what_it_does: Atlassian Rovo agents are AI-powered, configurable teammates integrated into the Atlassian ecosystem that automate repetitive tasks and execute complex workflows across Jira, Confluence, and connected third-party tools. They utilize organizational knowledge and user-defined instructions to perform actions like triaging tickets, summarizing content, and streamlining cross-platform collaboration.

incidents_or_risks.what: RovoBlast: one-click flaw (Varonis) in which a crafted link using the rovoChatPrompt parameter preloaded attacker instructions into a logged-in user's Rovo Chat, enabling collection and outbound transfer of Jira, Confluence, and SharePoint data. Varonis reported that the link-parameter flaw was remediated server-side on July 8, 2026.
incidents_or_risks.when: Disclosed around DEF CON, August 2026; remediation July 8, 2026

incidents_or_risks.what: Indirect prompt injection (PromptArmor): hidden instructions in an uploaded document led Rovo to gather Jira and Confluence data and send it to an attacker-controlled URL. The researchers said the chain still worked with the organization's web-search option switched off, and Atlassian had not provided further communication at publication.

Atlassian's disabling of the web-search toggle did not remove Rovo's URL-retrieval capability, so the toggle alone is not a complete boundary against outbound data flows, per analysis of the PromptArmor finding.
No CVE had been assigned to these techniques, and the researchers reported no evidence of exploitation against a live customer environment.
incidents_or_risks.when: As of the August 2026 CSA research note

incidents_or_risks.what: Atlassian's own best-practices material says agents can be manipulated by malicious inputs and that guardrail instructions are suggestions; automation-triggered agents have no user present to approve actions.
Data leaving Atlassian through third-party MCP servers is not covered by Atlassian's customer agreement commitments, and Atlassian does not guarantee the security of third-party MCP servers.

facts.claim: Rovo agents are described by Atlassian as configurable AI teammates that any team member can call on or create, and they draw on Atlassian apps and connected third-party apps.
Agent skills are the actions an agent is allowed to take, such as drafting a Confluence page or sending Slack messages, while knowledge is the data it can reference.
Atlassian's documentation says agents can be configured with knowledge sources such as Confluence, Jira, and Google Drive, plus deep research or web search.

Administrators can block Rovo for supported apps, which disables Agents and Chat for that app, though Rovo Search, Chat and Create remain available while any Jira app on the site still has Rovo enabled.
Turning off AI in an Atlassian site leaves core search and Studio working, but Rovo Chat and Rovo agents become unavailable.
A Rovo agent's actions depend on the user who triggers it, and Rovo searches only information that user can already access.
By default, everyone in an organization can create agents, and administrators can audit actions taken with Rovo through an audit log.
Atlassian states that Rovo agents are powered by large language models from OpenAI and Google, plus open-source models, and that Chat adds Anthropic models via AWS Bedrock.
Atlassian says it retains Chat and agent inputs and outputs for 30 days for safety and security purposes, and that its third-party LLM partners operate under zero data retention agreements.

Full Rovo AI features, including agents, require an Atlassian Cloud Premium or Enterprise plan, while a separate source says Rovo is enabled by default on Standard, Premium, and Enterprise plans; the two sources conflict.
A compilation of Atlassian's public disclosures reports Rovo surpassing five million monthly active users and completing 2.4 million agent automations over six months.
Rovo agents can be assigned Jira work items or tagged in comments, and in automation rules an agent can act asynchronously in response to Atlassian app events or schedules.
